mainTopic: The eighteen decrees, the three personal disputes of שמאי and הלל, and who made the decree on ארץ העמים and glass
overview: The amud opens by finishing an earlier answer: שלמה decreed טומאת ידים for קדשים, and later שמאי and הלל extended it to תרומה. Next, רב יהודה in the name of שמואל says the Sages argued about the eighteen decrees. A ברייתא seems to say they agreed, and the גמרא answers that they argued on the day of the vote and all agreed the next day. רב הונא then says שמאי and הלל themselves disagreed in only three places: the minimum dough for חלה, how much drawn water ruins a מקוה, and how far back a woman who finds blood becomes טמאה. In the מקוה case, two weavers bring a tradition from שמעיה and אבטליון, and the Sages accept it. The גמרא challenges the count of three with two more disputes, סמיכה and grapes picked for the press. It answers that סמיכה was already argued by earlier generations, and that in the grape case הלל gave in. Finally, the גמרא asks how the first זוג could have made the decrees on ארץ העמים and glass. A tradition from רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי dates them to the last 80 years before the חורבן, and the two יוסי's lived long before then. Along the way, the גמרא explains that the סנהדרין stopped judging capital cases once it left its chamber. The question about the two יוסי's continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שלמה decreed for קדשים; later Sages extended it to תרומה
steps.stepSummary: This closes an earlier answer. שלמה made the decree on hands only for קדשים. שמאי and הלל came later and widened it to include תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: שלמה decreed impurity of hands for קדשים, and they (שמאי, הלל and their students) came and decreed it even for תרומה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes answering an earlier question: who made the decree about impure hands, שלמה or שמאי and הלל? Its answer is that both did, each at a different level.
steps.deeperAnalysis: On the previous amud, the גמרא had two sources that seemed to contradict each other about who made the hands decree. The answer splits the decree into two layers. שלמה made it for holy offerings, and the later Sages expanded it to תרומה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This shows a common pattern: a decree can start narrow and be widened by later generations, so two sources can both be right about who made it.

phrases.english: Solomon decreed for consecrated items,
and they came and decreed even for terumah.
phrases.notes: 'אינהו' (they) refers to שמאי, הלל and their students.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes an answer that began on the previous amud.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting into stages: two decrees at two levels, made by two different authorities.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: It looked as if the hands decree was credited to two different authorities in a way that contradicts.
steps.terutzMaskana: שלמה decreed for קדשים, and שמאי and הלל extended it to תרומה.

steps.title: Eighteen decrees, made after eighteen disagreements
steps.stepSummary: רב יהודה, quoting שמואל, says the Sages made eighteen decrees and had disagreed about those same eighteen matters.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for the matter itself: רב יהודה said that שמואל said: they decreed eighteen things, and about those eighteen they disagreed.
steps.whatsHappening: The word 'גופא' tells us the גמרא is going back to a statement it quoted earlier in passing, so it can now look at it directly. That statement is that eighteen decrees were made after a disagreement.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The eighteen decrees (י"ח דבר) were passed on one famous day in the attic of חנניה בן חזקיה. שמואל adds that these decrees were not unanimous; the Sages argued about them first. This sets up the next step, where a ברייתא seems to say the opposite.

keyTerms.meaning: 'the matter itself': returning to look at a statement quoted earlier

phrases.english: The matter itself:
Rav Yehuda said that Shmuel said:
They decreed eighteen things,
and about those eighteen they disagreed.

steps.triggerLanguage: גּוּפָא, אָמַר רַב יְהוּדָה אָמַר שְׁמוּאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section by returning to a statement quoted earlier.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The eighteen decrees were passed only after the Sages disagreed about them.

steps.title: A ברייתא says they agreed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges שמואל with a ברייתא that says the Sages reached agreement about the eighteen decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: they agreed?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks שמואל's statement. A ברייתא says 'הושוו', meaning they were all in agreement, which seems to contradict 'נחלקו', they disagreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two sources seem to describe the eighteen decrees in opposite ways. One says they were argued over, and the other says everyone agreed. Both cannot be true unless they describe different moments.

keyTerms.meaning: 'But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?': introduces a challenge from a ברייתא
they were made equal, meaning they reached agreement

phrases.english: But wasn't it taught: they agreed?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges step 2.
steps.kashyaTarget: שמואל's statement that they disagreed (נחלקו) about the eighteen.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A ברייתא says they agreed (הושוו), which contradicts disagreement.

steps.title: They disagreed that day and agreed the next
steps.stepSummary: Both sources are true at different times. The Sages argued on the day of the vote, and on the next day they all accepted the decrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: On that day they disagreed, and the next day they agreed.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by putting the two sources at different times. The disagreement came first, and the agreement came the next day.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nobody is wrong. שמואל is describing the day of the debate and vote. The ברייתא is describing the following day, once the matter was decided and everyone accepted it.
steps.whatToRemember: The eighteen decrees were first argued over, then voted on, and then accepted by everyone the next day.

phrases.english: On that day they disagreed,
and the next day they agreed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge in step 3.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Splitting by time: the two sources describe two different days.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'Disagreed' and 'agreed' looked like they contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: They disagreed on the day of the vote and agreed the following day.

steps.title: שמאי and הלל disagreed in only three places
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא says שמאי and הלל themselves argued in only three places. This sets up the list that follows.
steps.simpleTranslation: As for the matter itself: רב הונא said: In three places שמאי and הלל disagreed.
steps.whatsHappening: Using 'גופא' again, the גמרא goes back to another statement quoted earlier. This line is a setup: the next steps list the disputes one by one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is that שמאי and הלל personally (not their schools, בית שמאי and בית הלל) had very few arguments. The גמרא now goes through the cases to show what they were.

keyTerms.meaning: the two great Sages themselves, not their schools

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up שמאי and הלל with בית שמאי and בית הלל. Their schools argued about many things. רב הונא is talking only about the two masters themselves. The three disputes are listed in steps 6–10: חלה, מקוה, and a woman who finds blood.

phrases.english: The matter itself: Rav Huna said:
In three places Shammai and Hillel disagreed.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new section, separate from the eighteen decrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי and הלל personally disagreed in only three places.

steps.title: First dispute: minimum dough for חלה
steps.stepSummary: שמאי says one קב of dough requires חלה, and הלל says two קבין. חכמים take neither view and say a קב and a half.
steps.simpleTranslation: שמאי says: from one קב, חלה is required. הלל says: from two קבין. The חכמים say: not like this one and not like that one; rather, one and a half קבין is obligated in חלה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the first of the three disputes: how much dough you need before you must separate חלה. The חכמים pick a measure in the middle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי is stricter here, since a smaller amount already requires חלה. הלל is more lenient. The חכמים reject both and set the amount at one and a half קבין.

keyTerms.meaning: the portion of dough given to a כהן

keyTerms.term: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה
keyTerms.meaning: not like this one and not like that one

phrases.english: Shammai says: from a kav, challah is required.
And Hillel says: from two kav.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה,
phrases.english: not like the words of this one and not like the words of that one,
rather, a kav and a half is obligated in challah.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first example of רב הונא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The halacha follows the חכמים: one and a half קבין of dough requires חלה.

steps.title: After the measures grew: five quarters of flour
steps.stepSummary: Once the קב became larger, the same amount was restated as five רבעים of flour. רבי יוסי says exactly five is exempt and a little more than five is obligated.
steps.simpleTranslation: Once the measures grew larger, they said: five quarters of flour are obligated in חלה. רבי יוסי says: five are exempt; five and a bit more are obligated.
steps.whatsHappening: This adds a note to the חלה ruling. The measuring units changed size, so the same amount of dough is now described with new numbers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The amount of dough did not change. Only the measuring cup got bigger, so 'a קב and a half' in the old units equals about 'five quarter-קבין' in the new units. רבי יוסי adds that exactly five is not enough; there must be slightly more.
steps.confusionAlert: The halacha did not change. Only the units did. The actual amount of dough stayed the same.

phrases.english: Once the measures grew larger,
they said that five quarters of flour
are obligated in challah.
Rabbi Yosei says: five are exempt;
five and a bit more are obligated.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Restates the חכמים's measure from step 6 in the newer units.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the new units, five quarters of flour require חלה. According to רבי יוסי, it must be slightly more than five.

steps.title: Second dispute: drawn water that disqualifies a מקוה
steps.stepSummary: הלל says a full הין of מים שאובים ruins a מקוה, using his teacher's wording. שמאי says nine קבין. חכמים agree with neither.
steps.simpleTranslation: And another: הלל says a full הין of drawn water disqualifies the מקוה (for a person must speak in his teacher's language). שמאי says: nine קבין. The חכמים say: not like this one and not like that one.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the second dispute: how much drawn water poured into an incomplete מקוה makes it unfit. The חכמים reject both opinions but do not yet give their own number.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A הין equals twelve לוגין, which is the same as three קבין. Because a smaller amount of drawn water already ruins the מקוה, הלל is stricter here than שמאי's nine קבין. The note 'שחייב אדם לומר בלשון רבו' explains why הלל used the unusual biblical unit הין: he was repeating his teachers' exact words.

keyTerms.meaning: and the other one (the next dispute)
a biblical liquid measure equal to twelve לוגין
drawn water, carried by people in a vessel
in the wording of his teacher

steps.whyThisMatters: The rule 'one must speak in his teacher's language' teaches that the exact wording of a tradition must be passed on faithfully.

phrases.english: And the other:

phrases.aramaic: הִלֵּל אוֹמֵר: מְלֹא הִין מַיִם שְׁאוּבִים
phrases.english: Hillel says: a full hin of drawn water
disqualifies the mikveh,
for a person must speak in the language of his teacher.
phrases.notes: This explains why הלל used the word הין.

phrases.english: Shammai says: nine kav.
And the Sages say:

phrases.aramaic: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה.
phrases.english: not like the words of this one and not like the words of that one.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the second example of רב הונא's list.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: הלל says one הין of drawn water disqualifies a מקוה, and שמאי says nine קבין. The חכמים reject both.

steps.title: Two weavers testify: three לוגין disqualify the מקוה
steps.stepSummary: Two weavers from the Dung Gate testify in the name of שמעיה and אבטליון that three לוגין of drawn water disqualify a מקוה, and the חכמים accept it as the halacha.
steps.simpleTranslation: Until two weavers came from the Dung Gate in ירושלים and testified in the name of שמעיה and אבטליון that three לוגין of drawn water disqualify the מקוה, and the חכמים upheld their words.
steps.whatsHappening: This settles the מקוה dispute. A tradition from הלל and שמאי's own teachers sets the measure at three לוגין, and the Sages accept it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The testimony carries weight because it goes back to שמעיה and אבטליון, the teachers of שמאי and הלל. The witnesses were weavers from a lowly part of town, which shows that in Torah a true tradition counts no matter who brings it.

keyTerms.meaning: the teachers of שמאי and הלל

steps.whatToRemember: The halacha is that three לוגין of drawn water disqualify a מקוה. A received tradition outweighed the opinions of even שמאי and הלל, and it was accepted even though it came from simple weavers.

phrases.english: until two weavers came
from the Dung Gate in Jerusalem
and testified in the name of Shemaya and Avtalyon
that three log of drawn water
disqualify the mikveh,
and the Sages upheld their words.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Settles the dispute left open in step 8.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: Three לוגין of מים שאובים disqualify a מקוה, based on the tradition of שמעיה and אבטליון.

steps.title: The third dispute: how far back a woman becomes impure
steps.stepSummary: שמאי says a woman who finds blood is טמאה only from the moment she sees it. הלל says she is טמאה back to her last clean בדיקה. חכמים say it is the shorter of 24 hours or the time since her last בדיקה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the other dispute: שמאי says, for all women, their time is enough. הלל says, from בדיקה to בדיקה, even if that is many days. The חכמים say: not like this one and not like that one. Rather, a full 24-hour period cuts down the time from בדיקה to בדיקה, and the time from בדיקה to בדיקה cuts down the 24-hour period.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the third and final item in רב הונא's list of disputes between שמאי and הלל themselves. The case is a woman who finds blood without feeling it start, and the question is how far back she is considered טמאה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: שמאי says she is טמאה only from the moment she sees the blood, so nothing she touched earlier is affected. הלל says we go all the way back to her last clean בדיקה, even if that was days ago. חכמים take a middle path: go back whichever is shorter, a full 24 hours or the time since her last clean בדיקה.

keyTerms.meaning: And the other one (the remaining item on the list)
Their time is enough: she is impure only from when she sees the blood
From examination to examination: back to her last clean בדיקה
From time to time: a full 24-hour period
Cuts down, limits the other measure

steps.confusionAlert: The חכמים are not saying 'always 24 hours' or 'always since the last בדיקה.' They are saying each measure limits the other, so you always use whichever period is SHORTER.

phrases.english: And the other one: Shammai says:
All women, their time is sufficient.
phrases.notes: Impurity starts only from the moment she sees the blood.

phrases.english: And Hillel says: from examination to examination,
and even if that covers many days.

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: לֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה וְלֹא כְּדִבְרֵי זֶה,
phrases.english: And the Sages say: not like the words of this one and not like the words of that one,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא: מֵעֵת לְעֵת מְמַעֵט עַל יָד מִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה,
phrases.english: rather: a full day cuts down the time from examination to examination,

phrases.aramaic: וּמִפְּקִידָה לִפְקִידָה מְמַעֵט עַל יָד מֵעֵת לְעֵת.
phrases.english: and from examination to examination cuts down the full day.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִידַּךְ, שַׁמַּאי אוֹמֵר: כׇּל הַנָּשִׁים דַּיָּין שְׁעָתָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes רב הונא's list of three disputes (חלה, מקוה, and now נדה).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: שמאי: impure from the moment of seeing. הלל: back to the last בדיקה. חכמים: the shorter of 24 hours or the time since the last בדיקה.

steps.title: Challenge: laying hands on offerings is another dispute
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks whether there really are only three disputes, since שמאי and הלל also argue about סמיכה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And are there no more? But there is the case where הלל says to lay hands, and שמאי says not to lay hands.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's claim of only three disputes. It points to a fourth one: whether one may do סמיכה on a קרבן on יום טוב.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא said there were exactly three disputes. The disagreement over סמיכה is a known argument between הלל and שמאי, so the count seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: To lean one's hands on the head of a קרבן (סמיכה)

phrases.english: And are there no more?
But there is: Hillel says to lay hands,
phrases.notes: On a festival offering, on יום טוב.

phrases.english: and Shammai says not to lay hands.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the count of three that the previous steps completed.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's statement that שמאי and הלל argued in only three places
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: סמיכה is a fourth dispute between them.

steps.title: Answer: רב הונא counted only disputes that started with them
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא meant disputes that the earlier great sages had not already argued about. סמיכה was argued by earlier generations.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רב הונא said this, he meant where there is no dispute of the great masters alongside theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that רב הונא counted only disputes that began with שמאי and הלל. סמיכה does not count because the earlier sages already argued about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The disagreement about סמיכה goes back to the earlier זוגות, starting with יוסי בן יועזר. שמאי and הלל were only continuing an old argument, so it was never theirs originally.

keyTerms.meaning: When he said it (he meant this specific scope)

phrases.english: When Rav Huna said it,
he meant where there is no dispute of the great masters along with theirs.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the סמיכה challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Narrowing the scope of the original statement
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רב הונא meant every dispute ever held between שמאי and הלל.
steps.terutzMaskana: He meant only disputes that started with them, not inherited ones like סמיכה.

steps.title: Second challenge: harvesting grapes for the press
steps.stepSummary: Another dispute is brought: whether juice from grapes picked for the press makes them susceptible to טומאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But there is the one who harvests grapes for the press: שמאי says they became susceptible, and הלל says they did not become susceptible.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second counter-example to רב הונא's count. This dispute is about whether the juice that leaks from grapes picked for the press makes them able to become טמא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This one was not argued by earlier sages, so the previous answer does not cover it. That makes it look like a real fourth dispute.

keyTerms.meaning: One who harvests grapes to take them to the winepress
Became susceptible to טומאה (through contact with liquid)

phrases.english: But there is the one who harvests grapes for the press —
Shammai says: they have become susceptible,
and Hillel says: they have not become susceptible.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A new counter-example that survives the previous answer.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's count of three disputes, even as narrowed in step 12
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Counter-example: הבוצר לגת is a dispute that began with שמאי and הלל themselves.

steps.title: Answer: הלל went silent and accepted שמאי's view
steps.stepSummary: The grape dispute is excluded because in the end הלל went silent and accepted שמאי's view.
steps.simpleTranslation: Except for that one, because there הלל was silent before שמאי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the grape case is not counted. In the end הלל did not argue back and accepted שמאי's position.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A dispute that one side gave up does not remain a standing dispute. So רב הונא's list of three lasting disputes still holds.

keyTerms.meaning: Was silent (did not answer back, effectively conceding)

steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's three disputes (חלה, מקוה, נדה) are the only ones that began with שמאי and הלל and stayed unresolved. סמיכה is older than them, and in הבוצר לגת הלל conceded.

phrases.english: Except for that one,

phrases.aramaic: דְּהָתָם קָא שָׁתֵיק לֵיהּ הִלֵּל לְשַׁמַּאי.
phrases.english: since there Hillel was silent before Shammai.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the grape challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Excluding the case because the dispute was resolved
steps.terutzHavaAmina: הבוצר לגת is a fourth lasting dispute.
steps.terutzMaskana: הלל conceded, so it is not counted as an ongoing dispute.

steps.title: Re-quoting the decree on foreign lands and glass vessels
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes again the earlier statement that יוסי בן יועזר and יוסי בן יוחנן decreed טומאה on ארץ העמים and כלי זכוכית.
steps.simpleTranslation: יוסי בן יועזר of צרידה and יוסי בן יוחנן of ירושלים decreed טומאה on the land of the nations and on glass vessels.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to an earlier line from the list of decrees and quotes it again. It is setting up a challenge that comes in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is not new information. It is repeated so the גמרא can question who really made these decrees.

phrases.english: Yosei ben Yo'ezer of Tzereida
and Yosei ben Yoḥanan of Jerusalem
decreed impurity upon the land of the nations
and upon glass vessels.

steps.triggerLanguage: יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה וְיוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹחָנָן אִישׁ יְרוּשָׁלַיִם גָּזְרוּ טוּמְאָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the הלל and שמאי topic and returns to an earlier statement about decrees.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The first זוג decreed טומאה on ארץ העמים and כלי זכוכית.

steps.title: Challenge: these decrees came from much later sages
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects that it was the sages of the last eighty years of the Second Temple who made these decrees, not the first זוג.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it was the sages of the eighty years who decreed!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the line it just quoted. It says these decrees were made much later, in the final eighty years before the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסי בן יועזר lived generations before those final eighty years. Two different time periods are given for the same decrees, so they seem to contradict each other.

keyTerms.meaning: The sages of the last eighty years before the חורבן

phrases.english: But it was the Sages of the eighty years who decreed!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the statement just quoted.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that יוסי בן יועזר and יוסי בן יוחנן made the decrees
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A conflicting tradition dates the same decrees to a much later generation.

steps.title: רב כהנא's story begins as the source for the challenge
steps.stepSummary: רב כהנא reports that when רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי was sick, the sages asked him to repeat teachings he had said in his father's name.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רב כהנא said: When רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי fell sick, they sent to him: רבי, tell us two or three things that you told us in the name of your father.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins bringing the source for its challenge. It is the story of what רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי was asked while he was sick, and the story continues next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sages wanted to preserve his father's teachings before it was too late. One of those teachings will be the source that the eighty-years sages made these decrees.

keyTerms.meaning: As he said (introduces a supporting source)
In the name of your father

phrases.english: As Rav Kahana said:
When Rabbi Yishmael son of Rabbi Yosei fell ill,
they sent to him: Rabbi,
tell us two or three things
that you told us in the name of your father.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins the source that backs up the challenge in step 16.
steps.raayaObject: That the decrees on ארץ העמים and כלי זכוכית came from the sages of the eighty years
steps.raayaSupportSource: רב כהנא's report of the teachings רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי gave in his father's name (continues next)

steps.title: The timeline sent by רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי in his father's name
steps.stepSummary: רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי sends the sages his father's timeline. 180 years before the חורבן, Rome took over. 80 years before, the decrees on ארץ העמים and glass were made. 40 years before, the סנהדרין left its place.
steps.simpleTranslation: He sent to them: This is what my father said. One hundred and eighty years before the Temple was destroyed, the wicked kingdom spread over Israel. Eighty years before the Temple was destroyed, they decreed טומאה on the land of the nations and on glass vessels. Forty years before the Temple was destroyed, the סנהדרין went into exile and sat in the shops.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the actual content of the report started in the last step. It is the proof that the decrees on ארץ העמים and glass came 80 years before the חורבן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The middle line is the key point for the סוגיא. It dates the decrees to the last 80 years of the Temple, not to the time of the first זוג. The other two dates belong to the same tradition, and the 40-year date about the סנהדרין is what the next question asks about.

keyTerms.meaning: He sent to them (he sent a message)
The shops or stalls on the Temple Mount

steps.confusionAlert: Do not mix up the three dates. Only the 80-year date matters for the question about the decrees. The 180-year and 40-year dates are extra details from the same tradition.
steps.whyThisMatters: This testimony is the basis for the challenge in step 16. It shows the decrees on ארץ העמים and glass came late, which seems to contradict the claim that the first זוג made them.

phrases.english: He sent to them: Thus said my father:

phrases.aramaic: מֵאָה וּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָרַב הַבַּיִת,
phrases.english: One hundred and eighty years before the Temple was destroyed,
the wicked kingdom spread over Israel.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָרַב הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: Eighty years before the Temple was destroyed
they decreed impurity on the land of the nations
and on glass vessels.

phrases.aramaic: אַרְבָּעִים שָׁנָה עַד שֶׁלֹּא חָרַב הַבַּיִת
phrases.english: Forty years before the Temple was destroyed
the Sanhedrin went into exile
phrases.notes: It left the לשכת הגזית, its regular chamber.

phrases.english: and sat in the shops.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the actual content of the report introduced in step 17.
steps.raayaObject: The claim in step 16 that the decrees on ארץ העמים and glass were made in the last 80 years of the Temple.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A tradition from רבי יוסי, passed on by his son רבי ישמעאל ברבי יוסי.

steps.title: What practical law follows from the סנהדרין moving out?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what practical difference it makes that the סנהדרין left its chamber 40 years before the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: For what law does this matter?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pauses on the third date and asks why it matters in practice. This sets up the next answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first two dates are clear history. But the move of the סנהדרין must have a halachic effect, or why would the tradition record it? The גמרא wants to know what changed in practice.

keyTerms.meaning: For what law? (What practical difference does it make?)

phrases.english: For what law [is this relevant]?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side question about the last date in the timeline.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The halachic result of the סנהדרין leaving its chamber.

steps.title: First answer: they stopped judging fines
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי answers that after the move, the court no longer judged cases of fines (דיני קנסות).
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בר אבדימי said: It comes to teach that they no longer judged cases of fines.
steps.whatsHappening: An אמורא gives a first answer to the question. He says the court stopped judging cases of fines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea is that the court's power depends on sitting in its proper place. Once it left, some types of cases could no longer be judged. This answer names cases of fines as what was lost.

keyTerms.meaning: An אמורא who answers the question
Cases of fines (set penalties beyond the actual damage)

phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak bar Avdimi said:
To say that they did not judge cases of fines.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: After the move, the court stopped judging cases of fines.

steps.title: Could it really be fines?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rejects the idea that fines stopped. Courts in ארץ ישראל kept judging fines for generations after the חורבן.
steps.simpleTranslation: Cases of fines? Would that enter your mind?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's answer. It says the answer cannot be right.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We know judges in ארץ ישראל judged fines long after the Temple was destroyed. So the סנהדרין's move 40 years before the חורבן could not have ended cases of fines.

keyTerms.meaning: Would it enter your mind? (This cannot be.)

phrases.english: Cases of fines — does it enter your mind?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that cases of fines stopped 40 years before the חורבן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Courts kept judging fines in ארץ ישראל for generations after the חורבן, so the move could not have ended them.

steps.title: Correction: they stopped judging capital cases
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא corrects the statement. What stopped was capital cases (דיני נפשות), not fines.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, say: they no longer judged capital cases.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא fixes the wording of רבי יצחק בר אבדימי's answer. The court stopped judging capital cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Capital cases may only be judged when the סנהדרין sits in its proper chamber. Once it left, it could no longer give death sentences. Fines did not need that chamber, so they continued.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, say (a correction of the wording)
Capital cases (cases involving the death penalty)

steps.whatToRemember: The סנהדרין left its chamber 40 years before the חורבן. From then on, it no longer judged capital cases.

phrases.english: Rather, say:
that they did not judge capital cases!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the challenge in step 21 by changing the wording.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The move ended cases of fines.

steps.title: The two יוסי's could not have lived in the last 80 years
steps.stepSummary: Someone might say יוסי בן יועזר and יוסי בן יוחנן were still alive in the last 80 years. The גמרא rejects this. A ברייתא says הלל's family led for the last 100 years, and the two יוסי's lived long before הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you say they were also there during the eighty years, wasn't it taught in a ברייתא: הלל and שמעון, גמליאל and שמעון held their position as נשיא for a hundred years while the Temple stood. But יוסי בן יועזר of צרידה and יוסי בן יוחנן lived much earlier!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to its main challenge from step 16. It blocks the easy answer that the first זוג was still alive in those last 80 years.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says four generations of הלל's family served as נשיא for the last 100 years of the Temple. The two יוסי's lived generations before הלל. So they could not have made decrees 80 years before the חורבן, and the contradiction with step 15 gets sharper.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you say (blocking a possible answer)
But wasn't it taught in a ברייתא?
The position of נשיא (head of the סנהדרין)

steps.confusionAlert: This step does not answer the question from step 16. It closes off one possible answer, so the question becomes even stronger.
steps.whyThisMatters: It proves the first זוג could not have been alive when the 80-year decrees were made. This forces the גמרא to find a different resolution next.

phrases.english: And if you say that in the eighty years
they were also there,
phrases.notes: Meaning יוסי בן יועזר and יוסי בן יוחנן.

phrases.english: but wasn't it taught: Hillel and Shimon, Gamliel and Shimon,
phrases.notes: Four generations: father, son, grandson, great-grandson.

phrases.aramaic: נָהֲגוּ נְשִׂיאוּתָן לִפְנֵי הַבַּיִת מֵאָה שָׁנָה.
phrases.english: held their office of Nasi while the Temple stood for one hundred years.

phrases.aramaic: וְאִילּוּ יוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹעֶזֶר אִישׁ צְרֵידָה
phrases.english: Whereas Yosei ben Yoezer of Tzereida

phrases.aramaic: וְיוֹסֵי בֶּן יוֹחָנָן הֲווֹ קָדְמִי טוּבָא!
phrases.english: and Yosei ben Yochanan were much earlier!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא בִּשְׁמֹנִים שָׁנָה נָמֵי אִינְהוּ הֲווֹ, וְהָתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the side question about the סנהדרין and returns to the main challenge from step 16 against step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The possible answer that the first זוג lived during the last 80 years and made the decrees then.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: הלל's dynasty led for the last 100 years. The two יוסי's lived well before הלל, so they could not have been active 80 years before the חורבן.
